whyChoose.title: Why Talk to an Attorney Sooner Rather Than Later

items.title: California's Filing Deadline
items.desc: You generally have two years from the date of injury to file a personal injury claim in California. That window can shrink to as little as six months if a government entity was involved, so it pays to know where you stand early.

items.title: Partial Fault Won't Shut You Out
items.desc: California follows pure comparative fault, meaning even if you were partly responsible for the crash, you can still recover compensation — it's just reduced by your share of fault.

items.title: No Cap on Pain and Suffering
items.desc: In ordinary injury cases, California doesn't limit how much you can recover for non-economic damages like pain and suffering, unlike some other states.

items.title: You Pay Nothing Upfront
items.desc: Attorneys in our network work on contingency, so there's no fee unless they recover money for you. That means getting help doesn't require any money out of your pocket.

items.question: How long do I have to file a personal injury claim in Fortuna?
items.answer: In most cases, California gives you two years from the date of the injury to file a claim. If a government agency, like a city or county road department, was involved, that deadline can be as short as six months, so it's best to look into it sooner rather than later.

items.question: What if I was partly at fault for my accident?
items.answer: California uses a pure comparative fault rule, which means you can still recover compensation even if you share some blame for the crash. Your recovery would simply be reduced by your percentage of fault, not eliminated.

items.question: Where do crashes tend to happen in Fortuna?
items.answer: Public crash records show that corridors such as S Fortuna Boulevard, Main Street, Rohnerville Road, and 12th Street have the highest reported collision counts in town. These are simply the roads that carry the most traffic and reported incidents, not a judgment about any particular road.

items.question: Does LawProactive charge anything to connect me with an attorney?
items.answer: No. LawProactive is a free service, and we are not a law firm. We simply help connect injured people in Fortuna with an independent attorney who may be able to assist.

items.question: Will I owe money if my case doesn't result in a recovery?
items.answer: Attorneys in our network work on a contingency basis, meaning they only get paid if you receive a settlement or award. There's no upfront cost to you for reaching out or having your situation reviewed.
